title: Contain proxy fan‑out causing hosted API 5xx/timeouts and runaway retries
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer-facing incidents over the last 48h show correlated spikes in 5xx and request timeouts for multiple tenants. When customers retried requests (client SDKs + partner proxies) we observed amplification that caused transient saturation on model workers and additional 5xx waves. This ticket coordinates investigation, immediate mitigations, and a staged patch to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Multiple mid-market customers reported intermittent 5xx + client-side timeouts. Aggregate telemetry: 3x baseline 5xx rate during bursts, 40% increase in active upstream connections, and queue depth on our inference routers rose beyond SLO thresholds causing cascading timeouts for other tenants. Customer impact: medium-to-high for affected tenants (support P1 escalations).
timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Pager alert - hosted-api:5xx-rate > 250/min across eu-central region.
2026-03-10 09:25 UTC: Triage call (oncall, infra, runtime) - observed connection churn to model pool; spike in retry attempts from edge proxies.
2026-03-10 10:10 UTC: Short rollback of proxy connection pooling change in eu-central (rolled back, partial reduction in 5xx).
2026-03-11 14:00 UTC: Correlate SDK retry patterns with missing idempotency header for streaming/partial requests.

2026-03-13 16:00 UTC: Implemented server-side dedupe for identical request bodies for 120s window in canary (10% traffic).
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC: Canary shows 70% reduction in retry-caused inflight amplification; roll to 50% traffic planned after validation.
root_cause: Primary cause is an interaction between a recent edge proxy connection management change and aggressive client-side retry semantics. The proxy change increased outbound connection concurrency and removed subtle backpressure behavior, allowing retried requests to fan out to model workers. Additionally, many clients (including older SDKs and partner proxies) were issuing retries without idempotency tokens, so retries were indistinguishable from original requests and could multiply load. A secondary contributor: our circuit-breaker thresholds were too permissive under multi-tenant bursts, delaying local shedding.
mitigation_plan: Immediate: rollback proxy change rolled back in eu-central (complete).
Short term: deploy per-tenant inflight caps and tighten router circuit-breaker thresholds (in progress).
Short term: require/normalize idempotency header for non-streaming requests and add a best-effort server-side dedupe for identical request hashes (canary deployed).
Medium term: update default SDK retry policy to include exponential backoff jitter, reduce default max attempts to 2, and document idempotency expectations in SDK release notes.
Medium term: add observability — per-tenant retry amplification metric, dedupe hit/miss, and a retry-loop alert that triggers automated tenant isolation when amplification > threshold.
Long term: enhance edge proxy to surface retry-intent header and reintroduce adaptive backpressure that respects downstream queue depth and model-level saturation signals.
rollout_plan: Canary: server-side dedupe & tightened circuit-breakers to 10% of traffic (complete, low risk).
Validation: monitor 5xx rate, inflight counts, and dedupe ratio for 24h (ongoing).
Gradual rollout: increase to 50% after 24h validation, then to 100% over 48h if stable.
SDK: publish SDK patch (v2.3.1) that reduces retry defaults, add idempotency helper, and update docs; coordinate with partners for staged client updates.
Escalation comms: publish incident summary and mitigations to affected customers and update status page with ETA for full rollout.
